findings.title: Strict top-exponent inequality does not guarantee global stationary-lift uniqueness
findings.location: Remark4.4(1), p14; paragraph below Theorem1.5 p4
findings.claim: lambda1(W)>alpha(bar_nu), with Theorem1.5 hypotheses and qualifying W', implies a unique lift on all P(V) minus P(W).
findings.counterexample: mu=delta_diag(2,1,1,1/2) on R4; W=span(e1,e2,e4); W'=span(e3,e4); bar_nu=delta_[e3+W].
checks: First moment log2; invertible diagonal action; all subspaces H_mu-invariant.
W' intersect W=R e4 is nonzero with exponent -log2<0, and W'/intersection exactly spans quotient.
For every real c, nu_c=delta_[e3+c e2] is a distinct stationary ergodic lift; g fixes every point.
Within fixed W', only nu_0 survives contraction y->y/2; its carrier R e3 is strictly smaller than W'.
findings.mechanism: The maximum exponent on W does not rule out an intermediate critical direction with quotient exponent.
findings.impact: False central global uniqueness guarantee; no refutation of Theorem1.5 existence, Theorem1.3 FKH-specific uniqueness, Theorem1.1 semisimplicity or Corollary1.6 orbitwise uniqueness.
findings.repair: For fixed W' satisfying strict intersection contraction, at most one lift concentrated on P(W') minus P(W' intersect W), conditional on existence. Carrier only contained in W'.
findings.repair_verification: Analytic stationary joining and projective-distance contraction in report Appendix A and helper checkpoint; general existence remains external.

findings.title: Strong irreducibility of ambient representations is insufficient in Lemma3.6
findings.counterexample: G=SL2(R), rho=Std, rho'=Sym2 Std, mu=delta_u for u=[[1,1],[0,1]]. Both ambient representations strongly irreducible; finite moments; equal exponent0. Norm ratio <=sqrt(n^2+2)/n^2 ->0.
findings.impact: Standalone lemma exceeds scope justified by proof. Actual connected Zariski-dense H_mu application has support-generated strong irreducibility and is not contradicted.
findings.repair: Require strong irreducibility of rho(Gamma_mu),rho'(Gamma_mu), or specify actual support Zariski closure in applicable setting.
findings.repair_verification: Necessity and compatibility with actual application checked; external norm comparison/Atkinson ingredients not independently re-proved.

findings.title: Positive infinitely-often recurrence assertion is false
findings.counterexample: V=R, mu=delta_2, g=2, O=(1.5,2.5). Unique product path 2^n visits O only once; limsup probability0. Critical, first moment and connected-Zariski hypotheses hold.
findings.impact: The intended semigroup equality survives; recurrence reasoning is invalid.
findings.repair: Approximate by finite support words returning to identity component; split at first return blocks; each block in supp(mu^tau) by positive open-neighborhood probability and locally constant finite coset itinerary; take products and closure.
findings.repair_verification: Exact analytic finite-word proof checked, no recurrence assumption.

findings.title: Compactness is only projective; unnormalized GL sandwich may be unbounded
findings.counterexample: V=R2, mu=delta_(2I), nondegenerate rotation-invariant projective probability, any line W. C(Gamma) nonnegative scalars; only nonzero idempotent pi=I. Any nonempty Zariski-open O includes all but finitely many 2^n I, hence unbounded sandwich; projective image trivial.
findings.impact: Literal GL compact subgroup assertion false, but needed invariant complement follows from projective compactness.
findings.repair: Normalize A by |det A|^(-1/d). Normalized projective compact closure has bounded singular values and inverse, is compact group; average inner product; scalar rescaling preserves invariant complements.
findings.repair_verification: Exact normalization and downstream equations3.10–3.11 checked.

independent_acceptance_review.summary: All four reported defects are independently confirmed with the stated impact boundaries. Remark4.4(1)'s global uniqueness and carrier claims are false under its printed top-exponent hypothesis; the fixed-carrier, at-most-one repair is valid. The other three defects are local and have compatible repairs. Neither the existence equivalence nor FKH-specific and orbitwise uniqueness is refuted.

problem_checks.assumptions: mu=delta_diag(2,1,1,1/2),V=R4,W=span(e1,e2,e4),W'=span(e3,e4),bar_nu=delta_[e3+W]. First moment finite; W and W' invariant; alpha(bar_nu)=0<lambda1(W)=log2;lambda1(W intersect W')=-log2<0;the quotient support is exact.
problem_checks.independent_derivation: Every [e3+c e2] is fixed, giving distinct stationary ergodic lifts for every real c. The lift in W' contracts y to y/2 and is delta_[e3], whose carrier is strictly smaller than W'. Maximum exponent on W leaves a critical e2 direction. For fixed W', a stationary joining over the common quotient exists by Cesaro averaging on the compact projective product; the marginals give zero mass to the removed projective subspace. Equal quotient representatives differ in Z=W intersect W'; strict exponent separation forces projective distance to0 almost surely. Stationarity forces the joining onto the diagonal. The quotient/ambient cocycle average equality follows by truncating log(||v||/||qv||), stationarity, and domination of increments by the first-moment integrand.
problem_checks.counterevidence_and_impact: This is a false global guarantee and an overclaimed carrier equality, not a counterexample to Theorem1.5 existence. The FKH filtration in Theorem1.3 and individual orbit in Corollary1.6 enforce different support conditions. The corrected fixed-carrier statement proves at most one conditional on existence.
problem_checks.repair: Restrict uniqueness to the chosen W' with strict intersection contraction; replace exact carrier equality by containment. Do not infer global uniqueness from lambda1(W)>alpha alone.

problem_checks.assumptions: Connected G=SL2(R),strongly irreducible ambient Std and Sym2Std,mu=delta_u,u=[[1,1],[0,1]]. Both finite moments and top exponents0.
problem_checks.independent_derivation: For u^n the standard norm is at most sqrt(n^2+2), whereas the Sym2 matrix has an n^2 entry and norm at least n^2. The ratio tends to0, so no subsequence has the stated positive lower bound. Irreducibility of the ambient G does not imply irreducibility of the support subgroup.
problem_checks.counterevidence_and_impact: The actual application uses irreducible constituents of connected H_mu, so its support-generated strong irreducibility excludes this witness. The standalone lemma is too broad; no failure of that application is established.
problem_checks.repair: Impose strong irreducibility on the support-generated actions or the actual Zariski closure. Compatibility is verified; imported Atkinson/norm-comparison theorems are not newly proved.

problem_checks.assumptions: V=R,mu=delta_2,g=2,O=(1.5,2.5). Finite moment, criticality, and connected Zariski closure all hold; the identity-component return time is1.
problem_checks.independent_derivation: The unique path 2^n enters O only once; its infinitely-often probability is0. For the desired semigroup equality, a finite support word whose total component is the identity can be split at successive return times. Small neighborhoods preserve the finite component itinerary and have positive product probability, so each first-return block belongs to the support of the induced law. Products and closure give the reverse inclusion without recurrence.
problem_checks.counterevidence_and_impact: The displayed recurrence statement fails under the actual reduction hypotheses. The needed support-semigroup equality survives by the finite-word argument.
problem_checks.repair: Use first-return decomposition of finite words and closure; delete the infinitely-often recurrence claim.

problem_checks.assumptions: mu=delta_(2I) on R2 with a rotation-invariant, nondegenerate projective probability and any line W. Theorem3.1 here does not require ergodicity. H_mu is Zariski connected; all exponents equal log2.
problem_checks.independent_derivation: The cone contains only scalar maps, so its only nonzero idempotent is I. Any nonempty Zariski-open set of the scalar algebraic group excludes at most finitely many scalar powers; the GL sandwich contains unbounded 2^n I. Its PGL image is the identity. For the repair, A -> |det A|^(-1/d) A is multiplicative and changes no invariant subspace. Projective compactness bounds the condition numbers; determinant modulus1 then bounds singular values and inverses. The normalized semigroup closure is a compact group, whose averaged inner product supplies the required invariant complement.
problem_checks.counterevidence_and_impact: The GL compact-group assertion is stronger than the actual proposition. Projective compactness suffices for the complement and equations3.10-3.11 after normalization.
problem_checks.repair: State projective compactness and normalize before taking a compact group and averaging.

independent_acceptance_review.source_scope: Exact arXiv:2305.02879v2 dated15 May2023,15-page author manuscript and matching frozen source files. No equality with a distinct journal version is assumed.
scope_and_limitations: Acceptance checks the reported findings, their assumptions and downstream uses, and the report's bounded coverage; it is not a new proof of every imported random-matrix theorem.
Lemma3.5(3)'s wording for arbitrary elements of Pi_b remains a scope clarification, not a demonstrated defect. The normalized limits and specific downstream products are distinguished.

The support-irreducible repair of Lemma3.6 still imports the named recurrence and norm-comparison results. General stationary-lift existence is not claimed to follow from the report's independent uniqueness proof.
